Also note that well aligned models are not sufficient to solve prompt injection by themselves yet. That said, we have solved prompt injection in practice when layering our latest models with prompt injection probes (on by default for all traffic) and auto mode (also on by default). The little bit of scaffolding helps.

https://t.co/z4jN6ip3cs
It's the little things https://t.co/dhyV5jPE8o
To all: this came out sassier than I wanted it to. I meant this post earnestly - this is an improvement, and it really is good that we are seeing that improvement. Please keep it up

Demand for Astra is really unprecedented. We're pulling all the levers possible to sustain the demand, but I've not seen anything like it until now and we went through very steep growth before. Priority will always be to keep excellent service for existing users, but we might have to pause new Pro subscriptions for a bit if this continues.
See you at the Astra party. Excited to meet some of you https://t.co/WOICELwSrQ

I am pleased to see that Ant’s new Claude Code has a version of background computer use on par with the version from Codex from last May this year. Nice work!

Shipping great features first turns out to be a great way to encourage other labs to ship too. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to shipping. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go!

We solved computer use in practice for GPT models about four months ago. But computer use is a significantly awesome thing no matter what model you use, and it is important that the industry similarly spends more effort to train their models to be great at computer use, among other elements of model capabilities.

As models become more capable and central to businesses and economies, the value of computer use only increases. We should be taking it seriously, and doing the right thing for our customers and the world.

Follow @roupenmd for more balanced takes from an actual oncologist (and AI enthusiast) on where AI is at helping to treat cancer. 

Hyping a "cure" without understanding basic facts is disrespectful to all the patients and family members suffering from this disease. https://t.co/Ocrr84RpRm

This kind of tweet is both interesting and misleading.

On the one hand, who doesn’t want a personalized vaccine that treats their cancer and reduces the need for chemo?

On the other hand, there are many patients and families desperately looking for treatment. 

Presenting this as what cancer treatment looks like in 2026 is just not true:

1. Promising results in melanoma don’t mean personalized vaccines work across all cancers.

2. A treatment showing promise in a trial doesn’t mean most patients can get it or benefit from it.

I’d love to hear from oncologists like @RoupenMD @jasonwilliamsmd:

1. How close are we to making personalized cancer vaccines a realistic option for most patients?

2. What’s still standing in the way?

items.subsection: What is factual from the tweets
items.title: 10,000 agents
items.summary: An OpenAI-linked claim circulated that a Navier–Stokes “solution” involved about 10,000 agents working collaboratively @ eknight .

items.subsection: What is factual from the tweets
items.title: Navier–Stokes existence/singularity problem
items.summary: Public readers understood the claim as concerning the Navier–Stokes existence/singularity problem , one of the Millennium Prize Problems , though the exact theorem statement and proof scope are not supplied in the tweet set @LearnOpenCV .

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Post-Training, and Serving Infrastructure
items.title: Harvey + Baseten’s M&A diligence work is one of the clearest model-harness co-optimization case studies.
items.summary: Their recursive language model (RLM) harness uses a root agent to search a data room, delegate to sub-agents for document review, and aggregate findings over corpora up to 80M tokens .

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Post-Training, and Serving Infrastructure
items.title: LangChain/deepagents shipped quality-of-life primitives for harness design
items.summary: , including subagent forking that passes supervisor context down to subagents, plus managed connections to abstract OAuth/token/consent flows for either agent-owned or user-owned identities @colifran_ , @hwchase17 , @caspar_br .

items.subsection: Inference and Systems: Sparse Attention, Agentic Serving, and Decode Megakernels
items.title: vLLM’s long-context serving work is notable.
items.summary: The project described Hybrid HiSparse for sparse-MLA models: KV stays on GPU while possible, then cold KV pages are offloaded to host memory , while a hot buffer serves the indexer.
